title: Read a maintenance notice without filling the gaps
summary: Build a first Copilot Chat prompt that extracts evidence and leaves missing details open.
requires: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat with the synthetic text below.
roles: Check the scope of a service announcement.
Turn a release brief into a checklist.
prompt: Using only the notice above, give me a table of affected service, start, end, time zone and owner. For each value quote the supporting words. Use “unspecified” when the notice is silent.

steps.title: Supply one short source
steps.text: Start a fresh work chat and paste this entire fictional notice. Keep the identifier so you can tell which version the answer used.
steps.help: If chat starts to summarize immediately, send the lab prompt as your next message in the same conversation.
steps.code: Notice A. Mail search maintenance, Saturday 09:00–09:30 UTC. Message delivery will continue.

steps.title: Extract the fields
steps.text: Paste the prompt. Compare every returned value against the single sentence that supports it.
steps.help: The affected function is mail search. If the answer says all mail is down, ask which sentence supports that claim.

steps.title: Change one fact
steps.text: Send a revised Notice B with the words “Owner: Taylor” appended. Request an updated table for B only.
steps.help: Only the owner and document reference should change. An invented owner for A means the evidence test failed.

check: A has a 30-minute UTC window and an unspecified owner.
B names Taylor. Neither notice describes a delivery outage.

title: Find the last confirmed instruction in a mail thread
summary: Use the chronology of a conversation to distinguish a requested date from a confirmed one.
requires: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat with the synthetic text below. Paste the mock thread directly; no email account action is needed.
prompt: Return three lines: last confirmed date, latest proposal, and person who still needs to respond. Cite the message numbers. Draft a one-sentence follow-up for the pending decision.

steps.title: Create the thread
steps.text: Paste these three messages together. The message numbers stand in for the links that Outlook can supply in a real thread.
steps.help: Keep the sender on each line. A proposal from an organizer and confirmation from an approver are different events.
steps.code:
M1 Approver: Tuesday is booked.
M2 Organizer: Could we use Wednesday instead?
M3 Approver: I will check.

steps.title: Check the status
steps.text: Send the prompt and inspect the evidence. Reading M3 in isolation leaves the prior confirmed date invisible.
steps.help: Tuesday comes from M1. If Wednesday is shown as confirmed, ask which message explicitly accepts it.

steps.title: Close the loop
steps.text: Append “M4 Approver: Wednesday is now booked. Cancel Tuesday.” Ask for the same three lines.
steps.help: Wednesday now has explicit support. The pending responder should disappear. Use the draft as text only.

check: Before M4, Tuesday is confirmed and Wednesday is pending with the approver.
After M4, Wednesday is confirmed and Tuesday is canceled.
sources: Microsoft · Copilot in each Office app

title: Write a release note for two audiences
summary: Use Word or chat to retell the same change without quietly widening its scope.
requires: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat with the synthetic text below. Optionally paste the fixture into an unsent Word document and use its Copilot pane.
roles: Translate technical changes into a help-desk note.
prompt: Write a 35-word user notice and a three-bullet help-desk note. Preserve platforms, time zone and required action. Mark unanswered questions explicitly. Use only the release note above.

steps.title: Give the editor precise facts
steps.text: Enter the release note below into a blank document or a new chat.
steps.help: If Word editing is unavailable, paste the same text into ordinary Copilot Chat and request draft text.
steps.code: Build 12. A display bug affects iPad only. Fix rolls out Tuesday 14:00 UTC. Restart the app after rollout. Windows needs no action.

steps.title: Read both versions
steps.text: Send the prompt. Highlight any statement about Android, downtime or a local time zone. The source says nothing about these.
steps.help: Ask for a revision preserving “iPad only” if the shortened notice says that all users must restart.

steps.title: Handle a missing date
steps.text: Replace the rollout sentence with “Rollout time pending.” Repeat the prompt and compare both versions.
steps.help: The old timestamp should disappear in both drafts. Look for the stale time in headings as well as body text.

check: Both first drafts limit the restart to iPad and preserve 14:00 UTC.
Neither revised draft invents a new rollout time.
sources: Microsoft · Copilot in each Office app

title: Recover a decision from a partial meeting transcript
summary: Practice attributing decisions when the available transcript covers only part of a meeting.
requires: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat with the synthetic text below. The supplied transcript substitutes for a licensed Teams recap.
features: Teams transcript scope, evidence and decision logs
roles: Separate a Teams decision from a chat proposal.
prompt: Produce a decision log with evidence IDs, owner and deadline. List unresolved proposals separately. Use “unknown” for anything outside the provided record. Do not assume silence means approval.

steps.title: Assemble the event record
steps.text: Paste this combined chat and transcript. The transcript begins ten minutes after the meeting starts.
steps.help: Preserve the source type. A chat message before transcription began can still be evidence of what its writer proposed.
steps.code:
09:03 chat C1 Lee: Could exports run nightly?
09:10 transcript begins
09:12 T1 Kim: I approve weekly exports.
09:13 T2 Lee: I will own the export job.

steps.title: Check the decision log
steps.text: Send the prompt. Compare the decision with T1 and the owner with T2. Note the missing deadline.
steps.help: If Copilot claims nightly exports were rejected by vote, ask for the vote text. This record supports approval of weekly exports.

steps.title: Remove the approval
steps.text: Delete T1 and rerun in a new chat with the shortened record. In Teams, this resembles a gap in the available speech evidence.
steps.help: The remaining evidence supports a proposal and an owner, while the approved frequency is unknown.

check: Initial approval is weekly, assigned to Lee, with no date.
Without T1, no approved frequency can be established.

title: Reconcile license assignments without counting people twice
summary: Use Excel or Copilot Chat to distinguish assignment rows from the people represented in them.
requires: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat with the synthetic text below. Optional Excel workbook for a formula or PivotTable.
features: Excel tables, distinct counts and reconciliation
roles: Count distinct mail users in a report.
Reconcile subscriptions in a small app.
prompt: From the supplied CSV, report assignment rows, distinct person-and-plan pairs, and distinct people. Explain your duplicate rule. Return the person list behind the last total.

steps.title: Supply four assignments
steps.text: Paste the CSV into chat or enter it in three Excel columns. Ask how the row ID differs from a person ID.
steps.help: Keep A and B for the first person. Those are two plans owned by the same person.

steps.title: Reconcile three totals
steps.text: Send the prompt. In Excel ask to see the source range and distinct list. In chat ask for the intermediate pairs as a table.
steps.help: The unique pairs are u1/A, u1/B and u2/A. Seeing only two pairs usually means the method dropped Plan.

steps.title: Introduce an incomplete row
steps.text: Append “5,,B”. Ask it to count the new row, flag the missing person, and exclude unidentified people and pairs from distinct totals.
steps.help: If the count of people rises to three, inspect the distinct list for a blank entry and restate the exclusion.

check: Four rows, three unique pairs, two people before the change.
After the change there are five rows, one exception and still two identifiable people.
sources: Microsoft · editing and verification in Excel
Microsoft · Copilot in each Office app

title: Build a slide whose headline survives the math
summary: Make a one-slide pilot report with a traceable denominator for each percentage.
requires: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat with the synthetic text below. PowerPoint with Copilot can render the slide. Ordinary chat can provide the slide text and speaker notes.
roles: Brief a steering group on adoption.
Share a beta survey with testers.
prompt: Produce a one-slide draft with a headline, two labeled fractions, and a speaker note about nonresponse. Cite the source label Pilot A. Count support among respondents and among all invited locations separately.

steps.title: Create the approved brief
steps.text: Paste the three counts, or save them in a Word brief and reference it from PowerPoint.
steps.help: Start with a single file if the presentation feature cannot find your brief. The chat fallback needs only the pasted counts.
steps.code: Pilot A. Invited: 12 sites. Responded: 9. Respondents supporting extension: 6.

steps.title: Build and check
steps.text: Send the prompt. Check that the slide distinguishes recorded support among all invited sites from support among respondents.
steps.help: Six of nine is about 66.7%. Six of twelve is 50%. The three silent sites have unknown views.

steps.title: Challenge the title
steps.text: Ask whether “Two thirds of all pilot sites support extension” is justified and request a replacement title.
steps.help: A suitable replacement identifies the respondent group or states the count directly. Speaker notes alone cannot repair a misleading headline.

check: The two denominators are labeled 9 and 12.
The headline treats no response as unknown.
sources: Microsoft · creating a presentation from a file

title: Check a mail queue against an explicit threshold
summary: Ask Copilot to classify observations using precise boundary and missing-data rules.
requires: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat with the synthetic text below. Excel users can put the sample into a small practice table.
features: Conditional formulas, missing values and boundary tests
prompt: Classify each observation: below 15 minutes is normal; 15 through 29 inclusive is watch; 30 or above is investigate. Blank or negative is invalid. Give counts, row IDs and a formula or pseudocode implementing the rule.

steps.title: Set up a test at each boundary
steps.text: Paste these minute values into two columns. Preserve the empty field for E.
steps.help: If a spreadsheet converts a blank to zero, check emptiness before applying the numeric comparisons.
steps.code:
ID,Minutes
A,14
B,15
C,29
D,30
E,
F,-1

steps.title: Check each comparison
steps.text: Send the prompt. Inspect which side of the 15 and 30 boundaries includes equality. Chat can produce the same truth table when workbook editing is unavailable.
steps.help: Read the formula from left to right. An invalid negative must be handled before “below 15.”

steps.title: Change exactly one input
steps.text: Replace A’s 14 with 15 and predict the counts before asking for a fresh table.
steps.help: Only A moves category. Watch rises by one and normal falls by one. Invalid and investigate counts stay put.

check: Initial normal 1, watch 2, investigate 1, invalid 2.
Revised normal 0 and watch 3.
sources: Microsoft · editing and verification in Excel
Microsoft · Copilot in each Office app

title: Resolve a migration policy conflict by effective date
summary: Reconcile two versions of a policy and keep special cases attached to the edition that established them.
requires: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat with the synthetic text below.
features: Multi-document grounding, exceptions and effective dates
roles: Track changes in a rollout playbook.
prompt: For each case A–D, return allowed, held or unknown; identify the governing edition and quote its relevant condition. Newer rules apply on and after their effective date. Identify unresolved inputs.

steps.title: Provide both policy excerpts
steps.text: Paste these fictional excerpts and cases into one chat. The dates here are unambiguous UTC calendar dates.
steps.help: If Copilot prefers the most recent edition for every case, ask it to decide which date applies before reading the eligibility rule.
steps.code:
V1 effective Jan 1: groups up to 20 may move.
V2 effective Feb 1: groups up to 30 may move unless flagged; flagged groups are held.
A Jan 31 size 25; B Feb 1 size 30 clear; C Feb 2 size 12 flagged; D Feb 3 size 12 flag unknown.

steps.title: Resolve the four cases
steps.text: Run the prompt. Treat a group exceeding the numerical limit as held for this exercise. Require the edition next to the verdict.
steps.help: D cannot be resolved without the flag value. If the tool assumes clear, ask it to name its evidence.

steps.title: Move only the effective date
steps.text: Change V2 to Feb 2. Re-run B and C. Compare the two decisions with their original results.
steps.help: B now falls under V1 and switches to held. C remains held under V2 because it is flagged.

check: A held, B allowed, C held, D unknown.
Changing the effective date changes B but leaves C held.
sources: Microsoft · Copilot in each Office app

title: Design a source-bound handbook assistant
summary: Prototype a reusable question-answering agent and test how it behaves when a policy is silent.
requires: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat with the synthetic text below. Agent Builder is optional and subject to your organization’s settings. Use chat for the same behavior test.
features: Agent Builder instructions, sources and evaluation
roles: Design a help assistant for an app.
prompt: Use only the two supplied policy clauses. Answer with a clause ID and the exact applicable limit, or say “not covered.” Ask one clarifying question when the item type is missing. Evaluate the three sample questions separately.

steps.title: Set the boundary
steps.text: Paste the clauses and questions. In Agent Builder use the prompt as instructions and a scratch document containing just the clauses as knowledge. Keep the trial private.
steps.help: If you lack builder access, put the instructions and clauses in one ordinary chat. This tests responses, not deployment.
steps.code:
P1 Standard archive request: 5 business days.
P2 Urgent archive request: 1 business day.
Q1 Standard archive time? Q2 Restore time? Q3 Archive time?

steps.title: Check the answers
steps.text: Run all three questions. Open each referenced clause and match its scope to the question.
steps.help: Q2 concerns restore. A confident “5 days” incorrectly carries an archive promise into a different service.

steps.title: Revise a source and retest
steps.text: Change P2 to 2 business days in the scratch source. Start a fresh test and ask for the urgent archive time.
steps.help: If it returns 1, confirm that the agent or chat received the revised source and repeat with a new conversation.

check: Q1 gives 5 business days from P1, Q2 is not covered, Q3 asks which request type.
Revised urgent requests take 2 business days according to P2.
sources: Microsoft Learn · Agent Builder and Copilot Studio

title: Calculate a rate across unequal migration batches
summary: Audit a success-rate dashboard and explain why averaging individual batch percentages can mislead.
requires: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat with the synthetic text below. Optional Excel practice workbook.
features: Weighted rates, recalculation and reviewer notes
roles: Measure adoption without weighting each group equally.
Track verification rates across app releases.
prompt: Report completed / attempted per batch, weighted overall completion, and the simple mean of the defined batch rates. Explain the difference in plain language. Treat a zero-attempt batch as undefined for its own rate.

steps.title: Create a small migration report
steps.text: Paste the data or build an Excel table. Ask for an overall formula using the sums of both columns.
steps.help: Exclude the all-zero row from the mean of defined rates. It still contributes zero to each overall total.

steps.title: Audit both interpretations
steps.text: Send the prompt. Use a calculator or manual arithmetic to confirm both results. Ask to see numerator and denominator.
steps.help: West is 90% and East is 50%. Their simple mean is 70%, while 82 of 100 attempts completed.

steps.title: Model an error in the export
steps.text: Change East completed to 22 with the original 20 attempts. Ask for validation before publishing any overall figure.
steps.help: For this fixture completions cannot exceed attempts. A helpful report names East, holds the aggregate and asks for corrected data.

check: Initial weighted rate 82%; mean batch rate 70%.
The impossible 22-of-20 row is identified before a final rate is reported.
sources: Microsoft · editing and verification in Excel
Microsoft · Copilot in each Office app

title: Audit a join that silently doubles your report
summary: Expose a many-to-many join before presenting Exchange or Microsoft 365 usage totals.
requires: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat with the synthetic text below. Excel is optional; pasted rows support the same paper audit.
features: Relational reasoning, join validation and exception tables
roles: Join player activity to customer records.
prompt: Treat each usage row as one mailbox. Count duplicate keys in the department map before joining. Report the trusted usage total, ambiguous mailboxes and their usage, and the total a naive join would produce. Never allocate ambiguous usage twice.

steps.title: Create two tiny exports
steps.text: Supply both labeled tables below. Units are GB for every row. Department mappings may be ambiguous.
steps.help: Ask for the keys in each table first. Usage contains two unique mailbox IDs and the mapping contains three rows.
steps.code:
Usage: m1=10, m2=20.
Map: m1→North, m1→South, m2→East.

steps.title: Inspect the inflated result
steps.text: Run the prompt. Request a row-by-row preview of a naive inner join and the sums before and after.
steps.help: The duplicated m1 contributes 10 extra GB. The 30 GB source total is the independent control.

steps.title: Clear the exception
steps.text: Remove the m1→South row. Rerun and ask which regional totals are now trustworthy.
steps.help: You should now see North 10 and East 20. If the total changes from 30, the assignment procedure has lost or duplicated a mailbox.

check: Before correction, naive total 40 GB; source total 30 GB; 10 GB ambiguous.
After correction, all 30 GB have one department.
sources: Microsoft · editing and verification in Excel

title: Reconstruct an incident across midnight
summary: Reconcile three clocks and avoid converting a sequence of events into a claim about the cause.
requires: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat with the synthetic text below.
features: Timeline normalization, evidence attribution and missing offsets
roles: Align service desk and application records.
prompt: Normalize each known timestamp to UTC. Make an ordered timeline with the evidence IDs, calculate the first-observed-to-recovery interval, and list unplaceable events separately. Describe what the evidence establishes about cause.

steps.title: Enter records with their offsets
steps.text: Paste the fictional evidence exactly as shown. The dates use January and the offsets are numeric.
steps.help: Use the supplied offsets for arithmetic. Inferring a time zone for a line that has none changes the evidence.
steps.code:
A Jan 5 23:55 -0600: delay observed.
B Jan 6 06:02 +0000: queue peaked.
C Jan 6 01:10 -0500: recovery observed.
D 00:59 offset/date unknown: configuration note.

steps.title: Check the day boundary
steps.text: Run the prompt. Verify A’s UTC date advances to Jan 6. Calculate the duration manually from the normalized times.
steps.help: A is 05:55Z, B is 06:02Z, C is 06:10Z. D cannot yet be positioned.

steps.title: Add time but not causality
steps.text: Give D the date Jan 6 and offset -0500, then rerun. Ask what proof would be needed to attribute the delay to D.
steps.help: D is now 05:59Z, four minutes after A. Its position alone does not establish that the note caused the incident.

check: The observed interval is 15 minutes across A and C.
D becomes placeable after clarification; cause remains unproven.
sources: Microsoft · Copilot in each Office app

title: Stress-test a readiness gate with stale evidence
summary: Turn a rollout checklist into a reproducible decision with failing and expiring prerequisites.
requires: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat with the synthetic text below.
features: Document-grounded decision rules and cutoff tests
prompt: Evaluate the gate at each supplied time. Report a row for every prerequisite, the exact evidence ID and its age when relevant. Overall result is GO only if all prerequisites pass. Mark missing inputs explicitly.

steps.title: Enter the fictional release gate
steps.text: Paste the policy and evidence. Treat “within 60 minutes” as inclusive.
steps.help: Require an explicit decision for rollback, backup and test status. Missing one row can make an unsupported GO sound plausible.
steps.code:
Rule: approved rollback; successful backup within 60 min; all smoke tests pass.
R1 rollback approved. B1 backup successful 09:00 UTC. T1 two passed, one pending.
Times: 10:00 and 10:01 UTC, same day.

steps.title: Evaluate twice
steps.text: Send the prompt. Compare gate status at the boundary and one minute later.
steps.help: At 10:00 the backup is fresh and tests are pending. At 10:01 the backup is also stale. Both evaluations hold.

steps.title: Change the test record
steps.text: Replace T1 with “three passed.” Evaluate both times again. In plain chat the verdict is a worksheet answer, with no release action.
steps.help: The result should change at 10:00 only. If both pass, ask for the elapsed minutes since B1.

check: Initial verdict HOLD at both times.
With every test passing, GO at 10:00 and HOLD at 10:01.

title: Simulate a request agent that receives the same form twice
summary: Specify how to handle a repeat request before any connector is allowed to act.
requires: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat with the synthetic text below. Optional private Copilot Studio design canvas. All actions in this lab use a paper ledger.
features: Workflow design, duplicate suppression and conflict handling
roles: Review an agent-driven service desk flow.
Protect a personal app order form from double submission.
prompt: Simulate a ledger keyed by request ID. New ID creates one draft row; same ID and same payload returns the existing row; same ID and changed payload flags a conflict without overwriting. Show every input decision and the final ledger. Perform no external actions.

steps.title: Prepare simulated inputs
steps.text: Paste the ordered requests. If using Studio, sketch the lookup and decision steps on paper or in a private scratch design. Do not connect a live system.
steps.help: The ID identifies a request. The name in the payload is not a reliable duplicate key.
steps.code:
R1 | project alpha
R1 | project alpha
R2 | project beta
R1 | project gamma

steps.title: Run the paper simulation
steps.text: Send the prompt and examine each outcome in sequence. Ask for the ledger contents immediately before input four.
steps.help: Two drafts exist then. Input four must flag a conflict without turning alpha into gamma.

steps.title: Test independence
steps.text: Append “R3 | project alpha.” Predict whether it is new. Explain what a real destination would need for two simultaneous submissions.
steps.help: R3 is a distinct request. A real implementation needs an atomic unique-key decision or equivalent destination guarantee. A chat simulation tests the rule only.

check: First four outcomes are create, reuse, create, conflict.
After R3 there are three rows; the original R1 payload remains alpha.
sources: Microsoft Learn · Agent Builder and Copilot Studio

title: Deliver a rollout brief that passes an independent audit
summary: Combine mail evidence, metrics and an approval rule into a decision memo and a single defensible slide.
requires: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat with the synthetic text below. Word, Excel and PowerPoint can hold the outputs; ordinary Copilot Chat can produce all three as plain text.
features: Cross-app synthesis, evidence checks and revision control
roles: Report a migration pilot with a defensible release decision.
Prepare an evidence-bound change advisory packet.
Publish a measurable beta exit recommendation.
prompt: Prepare a one-paragraph decision brief, a slide title and a verification table. Use IDs for every decision and metric. The gate requires at least 95% completed and explicit owner approval. Label unmet requirements and unsupported claims.

steps.title: Assemble the packet
steps.text: Paste each source separately, preserving its identifier. Ask for the two criteria before calculating anything.
steps.help: A proposed approval and an explicit approval have different evidentiary value. The gate requires both its criteria.
steps.code:
G1 gate: >=95% complete AND owner approval.
R1 North 48/50. R2 South 47/50.
M1 owner: I can review tomorrow.
M2 participant: We should move ahead.

steps.title: Challenge the headline
steps.text: Run the prompt. Check the totals and inspect which sentence establishes approval. If you use a slide, check its headline without reading the notes.
steps.help: 95/100 meets the numerical gate. Neither message approves. A defensible title says the metric is met and approval is pending.

steps.title: Retest two independent changes
steps.text: First add “M3 owner: I approve release.” Then revise R2 to 46/50 and ask for the updated decision. Preserve both versions as evidence.
steps.help: The first change unlocks GO at 95%. The second lowers the rate to 94%, so the gate returns to HOLD even with approval.

check: Original HOLD; adding explicit approval yields GO.
A 94/100 revision restores HOLD. All artifacts express the same decision.
sources: Microsoft · editing and verification in Excel
Microsoft · creating a presentation from a file
